original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-algebraic-stack-no-automorphisms}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be an algebraic stack over $S$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is a Deligne-Mumford stack and is a stack in setoids,
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is a Deligne-Mumford stack such that the
canonical $1$-morphism $\mathcal{I}_\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X}$
is an equivalence, and
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is representable by an algebraic space.
\end{enumerate}

Pinned-source scope: work over a fixed big fppf site $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Categories fibred in groupoids over this site are considered up to equivalence of fibred categories. A stack in setoids is a stack in groupoids whose fibre-groupoid objects have no nontrivial automorphisms. The inertia stack $\mathcal I_\mathcal X$ has over $T$ pairs $(x,\gamma)$ with $x\in\mathcal X_T$ and $\gamma\in\operatorname{Aut}(x)$; $\mathcal I_\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ forgets $\gamma$. A Deligne--Mumford stack is an algebraic stack admitting a surjective étale atlas by a scheme; an algebraic stack admits a surjective smooth atlas by a scheme. A morphism is representable by algebraic spaces when its 2-base change against every map from a scheme is equivalent to the stack associated with an algebraic space.
